title: Olive's Sound Game
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — alliteration and oral blending. Read this one ALOUD to the children.
note_for_grown_ups: An Introduction-phase book and the last one before letters begin. The last three pages are oral blending: YOU say the sounds separately and the children push them together into a word. Keep the sounds pure — 'mmm' not 'muh'.

pages.text: Olive knew a game. She would not say what it was called. She only said, "Listen to the beginnings."
pages.join_in: Olive. Owl. Oak. What do you hear at the start of all three?
pages.illustration: Olive the plum owl perched importantly on a low branch, one wing extended like a teacher, big amber eyes fixed on the reader. Two smaller birds sitting below her on the grass, attentive. Autumn oak leaves framing the page.

pages.text: "Pip," said Olive. "Pond. Pot. Petal." Pip sat up very straight. Those were all HIS beginning.
pages.join_in: P-p-p! Say the /p/ sound — a tiny puff, no 'uh' on the end.
pages.illustration: Pip standing tall and proud on a stone, chest puffed out. Around him, drawn small like a border, a pond, a flower pot and a single petal. Sand-and-gold palette to match Pip.

pages.text: "Ned. Nest. Nose. Nettle," said Olive. Ned checked his own nose to be sure it counted.
pages.join_in: Nnn! Say the /n/ sound and hold it — nnnnnn.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling going cross-eyed trying to look at his own beak, one webbed foot lifted. A nest, a nose and a nettle drawn around him in the same border style as the previous page. Funny.

pages.text: Then Olive changed the game. "Now I will break a word into pieces," she said, "and you will put it back together."
pages.join_in: Get ready — hands out, like you are catching the pieces.
pages.illustration: Olive holding one acorn in each foot and slowly pulling them apart, with a thread of light stretching between them. Pip and Ned lean in, wings and flippers out ready. Slightly magical.

pages.join_in: Push them together. What is it? (sun)
pages.illustration: Three separate acorn-shapes floating apart across the page, and behind them, only faintly visible, a warm round sun beginning to show through. Do not draw the sun fully yet.

pages.join_in: Push them together. What is it? (nest)
pages.illustration: Four pieces of twig floating apart in a curve; behind them the faint outline of Pip's ivy nest starting to assemble itself. Same visual logic as the previous page so children spot the pattern.

pages.text: "P — i — p," said Olive. And Pip fell right off the branch, because that one was him.
pages.join_in: Push them together. Who is it? (Pip!)
pages.illustration: Pip tumbling backwards off the branch with his legs in the air and an expression of total astonishment, feathers everywhere. Ned laughing. Olive entirely unbothered, still holding her acorns. Full-page, energetic, the funniest picture in the book.

pages.text: "Tomorrow," said Olive, "I will show you what those pieces look like written down."
pages.join_in: Tomorrow, that is you! Are you ready for the letters?
pages.illustration: Closing page. Olive scratching a single shape into a patch of bare earth with one claw — deliberately just a mark, not a readable letter. The three of them looking down at it together in the last of the light. Quiet, expectant.
